Text 1
Many nutrition guides recommend eating breakfast every morning, claiming that it improves concentration during the first hours of the day.

Text 2
In a recent study of adults, researchers found that skipping breakfast did not lower participants' scores on morning attention tests, although those who skipped breakfast reported feeling hungrier.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the researchers in Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1?
choices: By noting that their study found no drop in adults' morning attention when breakfast was skipped
By agreeing that eating breakfast clearly improves adults' concentration during the morning hours
By claiming that the hunger caused by skipping breakfast actually improves adults' morning attention
By recommending that adults eat a larger breakfast to reduce the hunger they feel during the morning
steps: Text 1 claims breakfast improves morning concentration.
Text 2 found that skipping breakfast did not lower attention scores in adults.
So the researchers would point to their result as evidence against the claim, at least for adults.
Their study doesn't support the claim, didn't find that hunger helps (only that it didn't hurt), and made no recommendation.
key: Base the response on exactly what the study found, no more and no less.
